title: Header Versioning
definition: A versioning strategy where the URL remains exactly the same, but the client specifies which version of the API they want by sending a custom HTTP Header.
simpleExplanation: You only have one URL: `/api/users`. But when you send the request, you attach a sticky note (Header) that says 'Please give me the 2022 version of this data'. The server reads the sticky note and formats the data accordingly.
realWorldExample: GitHub's API uses a custom Accept header: `Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json`. Stripe uses a custom Stripe-Version header: `Stripe-Version: 2023-10-16`.

basic: Which versioning strategy is easier for a non-developer to test in a web browser: URL Versioning or Header Versioning?
intermediate: What is 'Content Negotiation' in the context of Header Versioning?

answers.question: Easier to test?
answers.answer: URL Versioning. You can just type `/v1/users` into Chrome and hit enter. To test Header versioning, you must use a tool like Postman or write code to manually attach the HTTP headers.

answers.question: Content Negotiation?
answers.answer: It is the process where the client uses the `Accept` header to tell the server what format and version of data it wants, and the server negotiates to provide that exact format.
